summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: The package publishes to the public npm @servicetitan scope with a trivial 3-line ionicons re-export as its main entry, but its package.json declares a preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle with hex-prefixed identifiers, a rotating string array (WV8StW shifts elements), and a ~1000-entry mixed constants table — a heavy obfuscator.io/bun-compiled shape whose name ("math_init") does not match the package's advertised purpose of React components for mobile webviews. Fetching a non-Node runtime purely to execute an obfuscated payload at install time evades scanners that inspect only Node-resolved code, and the payload cannot be statically vetted before it runs on `npm install`. The trivial published surface, empty author/keywords, and use of the corporate @servicetitan scope for content unrelated to any legitimate SDK are consistent with a dependency-confusion attack targeting internal @servicetitan consumers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
